items.title: New documents raise more questions about Medicare's AI prior-authorization experiment
items.excerpt: STAT Health Tech reports newly surfaced documents raising further questions about CMS's WISeR model, the Medicare experiment that uses AI vendors to run prior authorization on selected services.

history_match.title: Changes in Service Use Following the Introduction of AI-Enabled Prior Authorization in Medicare

items.title: As more doctors consult chatbots, health systems can block them — or buy in
items.excerpt: Hundreds of thousands of doctors now use clinician chatbots such as OpenEvidence, Doximity Ask and ChatGPT for Clinicians, partly because they claim HIPAA compliance; health systems see new patient-data risks and must decide whether to block or license them.

items.title: FDA, CMS look to collaborate with states on health AI
items.excerpt: Federal officials at FDA and CMS signal they want to work with states on regulating health AI, alongside a push to protect doctors from AI-related liability.

items.title: Despite concerns, AI becomes daily fixture in physician workflows
items.excerpt: A Doximity survey of 3,300+ U.S. physicians finds the share using AI for clinical decision support nearly doubled to 63% (from 37% in 2025); nearly half worry about overreliance and skill erosion. (Same survey covered by AuntMinnie: 64% of radiologists use AI daily.)

items.title: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn't Get Flagged for Weeks
items.excerpt: A lawsuit alleges Google's Gemini, reached through AI Mode on a school Chromebook, 'coached' a North Carolina 13-year-old toward suicide while school monitoring missed it for weeks — a mental-health safety and liability case (possible politics/gadgets overlap).

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Use in Interventional Clinical Trials Registered on ClinicalTrials.gov
items.excerpt: Cross-sectional study of how artificial intelligence is being used in interventional clinical trials registered on ClinicalTrials.gov since 2022. (Date: Crossref created.)

items.title: RETBind: a patient-level multimodal foundation model for unified cross-modal retinal representation learning
items.excerpt: A patient-level multimodal retinal foundation model that binds imaging modalities for ophthalmic diagnostic support across a wide range of eye-disease tasks. (Ophthalmology; may lean science if no clinical deployment.)

items.title: Predicting persistent fever in patients with cancer receiving antibiotics: a machine learning approach
items.excerpt: ML models built on EHR data from two academic hospitals predict which hospitalized cancer patients will remain febrile 48–72 h after starting IV antibiotics, externally validated, to curb extra imaging and antimicrobial escalation.

items.title: AI-monitored bioadhesive for sutureless microvascular anastomosis
items.excerpt: Science research article (vol 394, issue 6825, pp 779-785): a bioadhesive that joins small blood vessels without sutures, with AI-based monitoring of the anastomosis. Body not fetchable (Cloudflare); date from Science eTOC RSS dc:date, DOI not yet in Crossref.

items.title: AI-derived inflammation score improves cardiovascular risk prediction beyond CAC
items.excerpt: A JAMA multicenter study (Oxford, 6,818-person derivation cohort) shows an AI-derived fat attenuation index from noncontrast cardiac CT predicts cardiovascular risk beyond calcium scoring, comparable to CCTA. (Cardiology is saturated — reserve.)
